changes: Persons, roles and relation confirmed: Nandalāla is the commissioner (likhāpitaṃ), son of Mukundarāya; both carry the title bhaṭṭa.
Purpose rewritten as a gloss: the copy was made for the study of the commissioner's own sons, grandsons and so on (potra stands for pautra).
Notes expanded: the scribe is not named; the work's name in the colophon (padyālayaśāstra) differs from the catalogue title; there is no date or place.

purpose: for the reading of the commissioner's own sons, grandsons, etc. (svasuputrapotrādipāṭhārtham)
notes: The catalogue lists Nandalāla Bhaṭṭa as the scribe. The colophon instead says 'likhāpitaṃ ... naṃdalālena', meaning Nandalāla had the copy made, so he is the commissioner. The actual scribe is not named. In 'svasuputrapotrādi', 'potra' stands for 'pautra' (grandson); the copy was meant for his descendants, but he is not explicitly called the owner. The colophon calls the work 'padyālayaśāstra', while the catalogue title is 'Vijayahalākhya'. There is no date or place.
